title: “Men of Color, To Arms! To Arms!” recruiting broadside
lede: A three-sheet Philadelphia recruiting broadside of 1863 that changes typeface on almost every line, from tall condensed gothics to spurred Tuscans and expanded slabs.
summary: Black-letterpress recruiting broadside with a dozen wood-type faces, every line centred. Philadelphia, 1863.

source.label: National Museum of African American History and Culture: object 2012.133

creator.name: Frederick Douglass and others (text); U.S. Steam-Power Book and Job Printing Establishment, Philadelphia (printer)

evidence.note: Inspected the NMAAHC photograph through its [Commons copy](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NMAAHC-2012_133_001_-_MEN_OF_COLOR_To_Arms!_To_Arms!.jpg) at 1518 × 3000 px. The copy is NMAAHC object 2012.133, printing ink on rag paper, 238.1 × 117.5 cm.

styles.note: A textbook wood-type broadside: centred lines, one face and size per line, display capitals in black, and small roman text between the big lines.

context: NMAAHC describes the object as a large three-sheet broadside that promotes the enlistment of Black men in the Union Army, printing ink on rag paper, 1863, and lists Frederick Douglass as author. [NMAAHC 2012.133](https://nmaahc.si.edu/object/nmaahc_2012.133).

The foot line names the printer: “U. S. Steam-Power Book and Job Printing Establishment, Ledger Buildings, Third and Chestnut Streets, Philadelphia.” The list of signers includes Frederick Douglass, Octavius V. Catto, and William Whipper.
observed: About twenty display lines are stacked and centred, and each spans nearly the full width of the sheet.

The faces change from line to line: very condensed sans-serif capitals (“MEN OF COLOR”, “FAIL NOW, & OUR RACE IS DOOMED”), a heavy slab with bracketed serifs (“NOW OR NEVER”), condensed French Clarendons with spurred serifs (“SILENCE THE TONGUE OF CALUMNY”), Tuscan-style letters with split serifs (“VALOR AND HEROISM”), and a very wide expanded slab (“STRIKE NOW!”).
Long condensed lines and short wide lines sit next to each other, so the width of the letter changes to fill the measure.
Small roman and bold text runs as one or two full-width lines between the display lines.
Black ink on off-white rag paper. There is no second colour, no image, and no ornament except one rule above the imprint.
Ink coverage is uneven in the large letters, with grain and lighter patches, and the sheet joins are visible.
The names of the signers sit in seven columns at the foot, in small bold roman.
interpretation: The broadside shows the poster grammar at its plainest: no pictures, only a ladder of lines in which the face, width, and size carry the emphasis. Each slogan gets its own letter, so the reader scans from shout to shout.
The mix of condensed and expanded widths for lines of different length is the practical logic of wood type, which came in many widths of each style.
borrow: Stack short centred statements, and give each one its own face and width so that it fills the line.
Put one line of small text between two display lines to set the rhythm loud, quiet, loud.

images.alt: Tall black-and-white letterpress broadside. Centred lines of capitals in many different heavy typefaces read Men of Color, To Arms! To Arms!, Now or Never, Three Years' Service!, Valor and Heroism, We Appeal to You!, and Strike Now!, with small text lines between them and columns of names at the foot.

rights.statement: Commons tags the file {{PD-US-expired}} and names the NMAAHC object page as source. The broadside was published in the United States in 1863, and Frederick Douglass died in 1895.
